```text
Peak Poker Performance

Jonathan’s Comments
It is vitally important that you learn to defuse your thoughts if you want
to be a successful poker player. Before I make any significant decision at
or away from the table, I always ask myself why I am about to make that
decision and spend a few seconds ensuring my decision is reasonable.
Getting into this habit will ensure you have spent at least a few seconds
weighing the costs and benefits of your actions. Especially if your game is
fast-paced, it is easy to fall into the bad habit of making instantaneous
decisions; to maximize your equity, always weigh your options.
    It is amazing how often players make instant actions simply because
they feel a specific way about their current situation. I am sure you have
seen players who are on tilt who mindlessly spew their chips for no logical
reason. They are upset about the past and their ignorant thoughts direct
them to behave by bluffing off their stack. You rarely see someone who
practices mindfulness make egregious errors based on their emotions.
    Students frequently approach me with the problem that they always
think their opponent is bluffing. Others students think their opponent al-
ways has the nuts. A common leak of many players is they project their
strategies onto their opponents. The fact that you may frequently bluff
does not mean that your opponent does. If you assume your opponent is
playing in a different manner than he actually is, you will make costly mis-
takes. You must learn to recognize and utilize the important information
taking place in reality, not the irrelevant thoughts that pop into your head.
    I must admit that my head is not always clear when I am playing poker.
Random thoughts such as “I need to send Dan an email” or “I wonder what
my wife is doing” often arise. When this happens, I either write down
what I need to do so I remember to take care of it later, away from the
table, or I acknowledge the thought and move on playing productive
poker. I do not wonder what my wife is doing, relive our awesome wed-
ding and honeymoon, then text her to say “Hi!” Sorry Amie! If you let
every thought that pops into your mind direct your actions, you will fail to
live up to your full potential. Make a point to act on the workable
thoughts and defuse the rest.
```

```text
                       Neuropsychology and Peak Poker Performance

information that are readily applicable to poker. We are currently in the
golden age of brain research. Just a few years ago, we were technologi-
cally limited when peering inside the human skull. At the time, the idea
that your brain was fixed at birth and could not be changed became en-
trenched. Today, scientists are able to study living brains in action by us-
ing technology like functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) ma-
chines or positron emission tomography (PET) scans; what has been dis-
covered is game changing.
   Most people think of the brain as some undefined mass that somehow
warehouses memories and experiences, and mysteriously controls all our
actions and reactions. The brain is actually a complex system of structures
that interconnects and makes you who you are. Your brain weighs a not so
hefty three pounds, and is roughly the consistency of tofu or soft butter.
Even though it is only the size of a grapefruit, it is an energy hog that re-
quires about 25% of all the calories you ingest to operate. It also consumes
20% of the oxygen you breathe and 25% of your body’s total blood flow.
Your brain works tirelessly around the clock, even while you sleep.
   We now know that the brain is fairly malleable and changeable, a trait
known as plasticity: your brain can change as its cells connect in response
to experience. Whether we are reading, watching poker videos, or playing
actual hands, our dynamic brain is forging new connections. After giving
you a glimpse into some of the brain science most relevant to poker, I’ll
give you practical strategies that you can use to optimize your brain.
   If you truly want to bring your A game more often you must learn how
your brain operates, which will allow you to understand how downward
spirals devolve into sub-optimal performances, and how you can optimize
for upward spirals of poker success. Every mood, behavior, and thought
you have originates in your brain, and you can take steps to optimize
them. Even if you’ve had serious tilt problems or have lacked focus in the
past, we now have solid research that shows we can modify different
brain circuits, change the levels of various neurochemicals, and even grow
new brain cells. We like to imagine that our mental “stuff” is separate
from our biology, but the moods, ideas, and impulses that run through our
```

```text
Peak Poker Performance

minds are intimately intertwined with our biological conditions. So, to un-
derstand how the mind works and optimize the process, learn how your
brain chemistry influences how you think, feel, and sense things about
poker (and everything else)!
   It’s a myth that great poker players are born hardwired for success.
Brain changes are based on what you choose to do with it, and you have a
certain amount of control over how it develops. This chapter will teach
you how to have a more effective poker brain. Even if you require exten-
sive rewiring, it is well within your reach.
   There are many ways to shape your brain to express your genetic po-
tential more fully (a process called nurtured nature). Your brain is incredi-
bly adaptable, and its structure and function changes over time, whether
you give it direction or not. So, why not take the reins and optimize it for
peak performance? There are endless opportunities for improvement. You
can adapt the way your brain operates by consciously directing your
thoughts, emotions, and behaviors in a specific direction. How you think
and behave changes your brain, and changes in your brain further affect
your thoughts and behavior.
   Even if you’ve never tried to harness the power of your brain, you have
the capacity to transform your thoughts, emotions, behaviors, and even
the physical structure of your brain. If you follow the advice presented in
this book, you will be able to reshape, develop, and optimize the neuro-
cognitive characteristics that are essential for success. No matter where
you are starting from, you have the power to change your brain!
```

```text
The Exterior Brain
The Cortex
The outermost part of your brain is called the cortex. It is a sheet of cells
one-tenth of an inch thick, which develops so extensively that it folds in
on itself hundreds of times. This is what gives the outer portion of the
brain its cauliflower-like appearance. The brain structures mentioned be-
low are all under the cortex, which is where all higher cognition takes
place. Memory, attention, perceptual awareness, thought, language, and
the ability to make decisions occur because you have a well-developed
cortex.
   Although no two brains are exactly alike, we all have the same four
lobes in our right and left hemispheres. Each lobe is specialized to under-
take certain functions. The individual lobes contain billions of cells called
```

```text
Frontal Lobes




                        Figure 4: The frontal lobes

   As the name implies, your frontal lobes are at the front of your brain,
and the section right behind your forehead is called the prefrontal cortex.
We will spend more time on the prefrontal cortex later, because it is the
most important part of your frontal lobes. For now, note that the frontal
lobe is your executive command center. This is where planning, thinking,
and problem solving occur. Working memory, which is like your brain’s
scratch pad, resides here, so this is the area of the brain where focus hap-
pens. Damage to the frontal lobe can cause dramatic behavioral and per-
sonality changes.
```
